Harold Wood Primary School
Working together. Learning Together. Respecting each other, to REACH our personal best!.
School Events
Welcome to all Children, Parents and Carers to Harold Wood Primary School
On behalf of the staff, pupils and Governors I would like to welcome you and your family to Harold Wood Primary School.
Pastoral Support
We recognise the importance of providing pastoral care for our children.
Individual Needs
Each pupil at Harold Wood Primary School is valued as a unique individual.
Safeguarding
Our school is committed to the safeguarding of children.
Relationships and Behaviour
We want our school to be a happy and positive place.
Harold Wood Primary School
We strongly believe that school is a partnership between children, parents, teachers and governors, and that by working together we can enable and motivate children to succeed in all areas of development.
Our Vision Statement
Working together. Learning together. Respecting each other. To REACH our personal best!
Respect
Equality
Achievment
Curiosity
Respect
We aim to guide all our children to develop honesty, sensitivity, good manners and respect for others and the environment.
Equality
At Harold Wood Primary School we value all individuals and the contribution they have to make. All individuals are entitled to respect and equality of opportunity regardless of race, culture, gender, religious beliefs, age, ability, sexual orientation or appearance.
Achievment
We aim for Harold Wood Primary School to be a place where partnership and teamwork lead to high quality outcomes for all.
Curiosity
We aim to develop a child’s curiosity and enthusiasm for learning by offering a broad and balanced curriculum.
Healthy
At Harold Wood Primary School, we work together to be physically, mentally and socially healthy. We believe promoting good health and teaching children how to lead healthier lives, will lead to greater happiness.

Values and Ethos
Our school core values are Respect, Equality, Achievement, Curiosity and Healthy. These are essential qualities that we wish to instil in all our children as we prepare them for life in modern Britain.

About Us
Harold Wood Primary School
Welcome to the online home of Harold Wood Primary School. Harold Wood Primary School is a 3-form entry community primary school catering for children aged from 4 to 11 years, situated in Harold Wood in the London Borough of Havering.
We have a clear vision for our pupils:
'Working together. Learning together. Respecting each other. To REACH our personal best'We believe each and every child is uniquely talented and capable of achieving great things.
We believe each and every child is uniquely talented and capable of achieving great things. As a result of this, we strive to offer every child the best possible learning experience. Our children's wellbeing, safety and development is at the heart of everything we do. Our governors play an important supportive role, with each one adopting a responsibility and interest in particular areas of school life. Harold Wood Primary School is a school with many dimensions. We are proud of our dedicated, caring staff who provide the children with a sound framework of education whilst encompassing the requirements of the National Curriculum and all that it entails. If you would like any more information about our school, I encourage you to come and visit us or use the 'contact us' feature. Mr S. Fryd Headteacher
Harold Wood Primary School
Harold Wood Primary School is a school with many dimensions. We are proud of our dedicated, caring staff who provide the children with a sound framework of education whilst encompassing the requirements of the National Curriculum and all that it entails.
What time does the school day start?
The gates open officially at 8:39am, but often earlier. The gates are then closed at 8:49am so children have time to get to class ready for an 8:50am start.
What time does the school day end?
The school day will end (from January 2024) at 3:20pm for all of KS1 and KS2. Children should be collected from outside their classrooms or designated area in the window from 3:20pm-3:30pm. For our reception class, they finish at 3:10pm.
Do you have a breakfast and after-school club?
Yes, we have a breakfast club that starts at 7:30am. Children will be provided with breakfast and a range of activities. We also have an after-school club that runs until 6pm where children will be provided with dinner and activities. Both clubs are run by our own staff on site.

Governors at Harold Wood Primary School
At Harold Wood Primary School, governors play a crucial role in guiding the strategic direction of the school and ensuring its success. They collaborate with the school leadership to set objectives, monitor progress, and make informed decisions regarding policies, finances, and curriculum development. Through regular school visits and consultations with stakeholders, governors provide valuable oversight and support to uphold the school's vision and enhance the learning environment for all children and staff.

Curriculum EYFS Reception
In the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum at Harold Wood Primary School, the focus is on creating a vibrant and nurturing environment where children can explore, discover, and lay the foundation for their time at Harold Wood. Through a blend of structured activities and lots of guided play, children are encouraged to engage in hands-on learning experiences that ignite their curiosity and spark imagination. The curriculum is designed to be fun, interactive, and inclusive, ensuring that every child feels valued and supported in their learning journey. The children also begin their phonics journey in Reception, learning through Read Write Inc. Through activities that promote social interaction, communication skills, and creative expression, children develop the essential building blocks for future academic success while fostering a lifelong love for learning.

Curriculum Year 1
In Year 1, the curriculum is thoughtfully designed to nurture the foundational skills and curiosity of our young learners. In English, children develop early reading abilities, explore phonics, and engage in creative writing exercises. The children continue to use Read, Write Inc. for phonics lessons and also prepare for the Year 1 Phonics Screening test in July. Mathematics instruction introduces fundamental concepts such as counting, basic addition and subtraction, and shape recognition. Beyond the core subjects, Year 1 integrates a holistic approach, incorporating activities that foster social development, creativity, and physical well-being. Through a blend of structured lessons and play-based learning, students are encouraged to ask questions, express themselves, and begin building a solid academic and social foundation for their educational journey ahead. The Year 1 curriculum is designed to spark enthusiasm for learning and lay the groundwork for future academic success.

Curriculum Year 2
At Harold Wood Primary School, the Year 2 National curriculum emphasises preparing children for the transition to junior school, fostering increased independence in their learning journey. Students engage with manipulatives to strengthen their mathematical understanding, delving into practical applications to deepen their skills. The children continue to use Read, Write Inc. for phonics lessons. However, reading comprehension takes a more prominent role, with whole class reading aimed at honing their ability to understand and analyse texts effectively. Through a holistic approach, the children in Year 2 are equipped with the necessary tools and confidence to thrive as they progress into Key stage 2.

Curriculum Year 3
In the Year 3 at Harold Wood Primary School, students transition into the first year of Key Stage 2, marking an important milestone in their educational journey. With a focus on building upon foundational skills established in Key Stage 1, Year 3 encourages children to become more independent learners. Through a diverse range of subjects such as English, Mathematics, Science, History, Geography, and Art, students are encouraged to explore and engage with learning in a more self-directed manner. They develop critical thinking skills, problem-solving abilities, and a deeper understanding of the world around them. With an emphasis on fostering independence, Year 3 sets the stage for students to take greater ownership of their learning and explore their interests with curiosity and enthusiasm.

Curriculum Year 4
At Harold Wood Primary School, the Year 4 National Curriculum is designed to engage students in a diverse range of subjects and activities. Students explore topics in English, Mathematics, Science, History, Geography, Art, Design and Technology, Computing, Music, and Physical Education. To enrich their learning experience, the curriculum includes planned school visits to museums, parks, and historical sites. These visits not only complement classroom learning but also provide hands-on experiences that deepen students' understanding of various subjects. Through a combination of classroom learning and real-world exploration, Year 4 children at Harold Wood Primary School continue to develop critical thinking skills, cultural awareness, and a lifelong love for learning.

Curriculum Year 5
At Harold Wood Primary School, we have designed our own rich and engaging curriculum that is tailored specifically to our children. By writing our own curriculum, we can ensure that what we teach is suitably challenging, engaging, modern and diverse.
We offer a wide range of before and after school clubs including dance, choir, language club, cookery club, world culture, netball, cricket, drama, Lego, football, craft, chess, drama, cheerleading, dodgeball, and lots, lots more to supplement our already exciting curriculum.

Curriculum Year 6
In the Year 6 curriculum at Harold Wood Primary School, there is a strong emphasis on fostering creativity while preparing students for the transition to secondary school. Through engaging activities in subjects like English, Maths, Science, and the Arts, students are encouraged to think critically, solve problems innovatively, and express themselves confidently. Learning is designed to challenge their imagination and nurture their creative thinking skills, laying a solid foundation for the challenges they will encounter in secondary education. Moreover, collaborative learning experiences and opportunities for independent exploration empower students to develop resilience and adaptability, essential qualities for their journey ahead.

Whole School Curriculum Overview
Yearly overview of our curriculum at Harold Wood Primary School.
We have developed a forward-thinking, culturally diverse, and skills-focused framework that equips individuals with the tools they need to navigate a complex world, appreciate different cultures, and contribute meaningfully to society. Our curriculum ensures that what we teach is suitably challenging, engaging and is tailored to our school location and its history.
We offer a wide range of before and after school clubs including dance, netball, cricket, football, craft, chess, drama, cheerleading, dodgeball, and lots more to supplement our already exciting curriculum.
Where National Curriculum objectives do not naturally fit our learning journeys across a term, these will be met as dedicated focus weeks.

Breakfast and After School Club
Wraparound care on offer at Harold Wood Primary School
Our Breakfast Club is a welcoming and nurturing environment designed to support families and ensure children start their day with a nutritious meal and positive interactions. Club starts 7:30am and children are offered a wholesome breakfast, which includes a variety of options such as cereals, toast, fruits, and yogurts. Engaging activities are provided to keep children entertained before school begins. These may include board games, arts and crafts, or quiet reading time. The staff at the Breakfast Club are attentive and supportive, helping children settle in and preparing them for the school day ahead. It serves as a convenient solution for working parents and contributes to a positive and stress-free morning routine for families.
Our Afterschool Club runs from 3:20pm - 6:00pm and is run by the same staff as Breakfast club. We provide a secure space for children to participate in various activities. A nutritious snack is offered to replenish their energy after a day of learning. The atmosphere is relaxed and supportive, allowing children to unwind and engage in both structured and unstructured activities.
Structured activities may include homework help, arts and crafts, sports, and themed projects. The Afterschool Club often aims to strike a balance between academic support and recreational time, offering opportunities for both learning and play. Outdoor activities, weather permitting, contribute to physical exercise and social interaction.
Together, these clubs play a vital role in supporting families and providing a holistic approach to a child's education and well-being.

Volunteering: Offer your time and skills to help with PTA events and fundraisers. This could involve tasks such as organising events, assisting with administrative work, or helping with communications.
Attend Meetings: The PTA meets regularly to discuss school issues, upcoming events, and volunteer opportunities. It´s a good chance to share your ideas and suggestions.

SMSC and British Values
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development and British Values at Harold Wood Primary School
SMSC stands for Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural development . We teach SMSC to children through various activities and experiences that help them grow emotionally, morally, socially, and culturally.
Spiritual Development: We encourage children to explore and develop their beliefs, values, and morals. This includes promoting respect for different faiths and beliefs, providing opportunities for reflection and mindfulness, and fostering a sense of awe and wonder about the world.
Moral Development: We teach children about right and wrong, fairness, and justice. Through discussions, stories, and real-life scenarios, we help children understand the importance of honesty, kindness, and responsibility. We encourage them to make ethical choices and consider the consequences of their actions.
Social Development: We support children in building positive relationships, understanding their roles within the school and wider community, and developing empathy and respect for others. Through collaborative activities, group projects, and opportunities for teamwork, we help children learn how to communicate effectively, resolve conflicts peacefully, and contribute positively to society.
Cultural Development: We celebrate diversity and promote understanding and appreciation of different cultures, traditions, and customs. Through exploring literature, art, music, and festivals from around the world, we help children develop an inclusive worldview and respect for cultural differences. We also encourage children to challenge stereotypes and prejudices and embrace multiculturalism in our school community.
Through a combination of lessons, assemblies, extracurricular activities, and special events, we strive to nurture well-rounded individuals who are confident, compassionate, and culturally aware, preparing them to thrive in a diverse and interconnected world
British Values refer to a set of principles and beliefs that promote democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect, and tolerance for those with different beliefs and backgrounds. Sports Premium
The PE and Sport Premium is a government funding initiative in England aimed at improving physical education (PE) and sports provision in primary schools. The funding is provided to primary schools to help them enhance the quality of PE and sports activities they offer to their students.
At Harold Wood Primary School, with the PE and Sport Premium we aim to:
1. Improved Facilities and Equipment: invest in better facilities and equipment for physical education and sports activities.
2. Professional Development for Staff: provide training and professional development opportunities for teachers and staff involved in delivering PE and sports programs.
3. Increased Participation Opportunities: expand extracurricular sports clubs, activities, and competitions within the school.
4. Promotion of Health and Wellbeing: implement initiatives aimed at promoting health and wellbeing among students.
